transcript:
Header: 2025-08-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~50m | Meeting: Weekly POC check-in - model portfolio signoff & rollback scenarios
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Caleb (Redwood CSM), Dr. Elena Park (LumenHealth Head of AI), Marcus Li (Data Engineering), Sonia Rivera (Security), Tom Hale (Product)

Summary (auto): Quick review of metric spreadsheet, agreement on pinning approach (major.minor pins), define fallback to smaller quantized variant and region-based routing for capacity, identify compliance gap for audit log retention.

[00:00] Jordan: Alright everyone, thanks for being on time. We'll run through the results and then get into the pinning/rollback playbook. Priya and I will own the technical bits, Caleb on success metrics and next steps.
[00:27] Dr. Elena: sounds good, we only have 50 so keep tight please. We've looked at the high-level numbers you sent.
[00:38] Priya: Cool. Quick note — the sheet has three model candidates: rwd-3b-v1, rwd-7b-v2-q4, and community-8k-v1. We measured median p50/p95 latencies and a small quality sample. The KV cache was on for half the runs and off for the other half; I included both columns.
[01:05] Marcus: small comment, the p95 looked a bit... higher in eu-west, is that expected?
[01:12] Priya: yeah we routed some jobs to our test region which had slightly older infra, that's on the spreadsheet — eu-west nodes were 2.5x slower for rwd-7b-v2-q4 under peak.
[01:30] Jordan: I'll flag that in the email. But main callout: cost delta between rwd-3b and rwd-7b-q4 is ~1.8x token cost for the 7b at our pilot mix, but quality improvements on hallucination were noticeable on the clinical QA set.
[02:01] Dr. Elena: by "noticeable" do you mean clinically meaningful? We need to be explicit for risk.
[02:09] Priya: Good point. For the sample of 120 clinical prompts, rwd-7b-q4 reduced incorrect condition mapping by 12%, rwd-3b had higher brevity errors — that said the community-8k produced fewer false positives but struggled on long context.
[02:40] Tom: So tradeoff is latency/cost vs safety/accuracy. We have budget for a small cost uptick if the error rate is lower.
[02:53] Jordan: Right, which is why we proposed pin strategy of "major pin" to model family (e.g., rwd-7b) and "minor pin" to patch levels only after validation. If there's an emerging regression we want automatic fallback to rwd-3b or the quantized variant that passes our guardrails.
[03:20] Sonia: For security is there a difference in audit logs if we fallback across hosted <> private? We need guaranteed request-level audittrace retained for 90 days.
[03:33] Priya: Hosted preserves the full trace w/ request IDs and token-level cost breakdown. Private can be configured to ship the same fields to your KMS and SIEM but we need to enable extended retention — that's in the SOC2 appendix. I'll attach the doc.
[03:57] Marcus: Also, latency SLO — can the autoscaler do instant fallback? If we pin to rwd-7b and it becomes saturated will the system route to rwd-3b automatically?
[04:15] Priya: Yes, we have smart routing policies: capacity-based fallback that considers model compatibility (same tokenizer) and region preferences. There's a short-circuit for steady overload where we will route to a compatible quantized variant or smaller family. That's what we tested in the soak-run last week.
[04:38] Dr. Elena: How do you define "compatible"? Tokenizer differences are the biggest risk for prompt/response divergence.
[04:45] Priya: good call. Compatible = same tokenizer + same output shape for tool-calls. If tokenizer differs we do a strict translation layer but we flag the outputs and fall back to read-only mode until validated. That flagging shows up in the audit.
[05:10] Jordan: Real quick, another operational suggestion — we recommend pinning at the major level for 30 days and only minor patches after canyon testing. Sorry, car-ness, can we — canyon? (laughs) typo, can we limit auto-upgrades?
[05:28] Dr. Elena: Yes, we prefer explicit upgrades.
[05:32] Tom: If we pin MAJOR only, how do we get security patches? We can't delay critical CVE fixes.
[05:39] Priya: We support exceptions: critical security patches can be auto-rolled to minor if you enable the curated security channel. Otherwise we put them through a canary on 5% of traffic.
[05:54] Sonia: That works if canary logs are separate and auditable. We need a report for any auto-rolled patch.
[06:04] Priya: We'll add that to the rollout notes.
[06:12] [06:12] Caleb: quick recap of the numbers — rwd-7b-q4 p50 = 140ms local, p95 = 480ms, cost/unit = $0.018 per 1k tokens; rwd-3b p50 = 90ms, p95 = 260ms, cost/unit = $0.01 per 1k tokens. community-8k p50 = 220ms but lower hallucination on prompt set A.
[06:45] Dr. Elena: On the usability side, we need deterministic outputs for certain templates. Which model gave the narrowest variance?
[06:55] Priya: rwd-3b had the tightest entropy on templated prompts, interestingly. The 7b is better on open-ended reasoning but more variable length-wise.
[07:10] Marcus: For the pilot we'd like to pin to rwd-7b for the clinical scoring pipeline but fallback to rwd-3b for patient-facing chat where determinism matters.
[07:25] Jordan: That's exactly the route-based pin we can do: per-route enforcement. We'll add a per-route fallback priority list and a roll-forward/rollback hook.
[07:40] Dr. Elena: Can you show a quick mock of the config?
[07:45] Priya: Sure — I pulled the example from the docs: route: /clinical-score -> pinned: rwd-7b@major, fallbacks: [rwd-7b-q4, rwd-3b@major], rollout: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with health checks. I'll share the snippet after.
[08:10] Tom: Any gotchas around tokenization with the quantized variant? I worry about scoring drift.
[08:18] Priya: Quantization doesn't change the tokenizer, but aggressive quantization can affect logits and cause subtle answer changes. That's why we run regression tests on your prompt set during canary. We recommend a small golden set for deterministic checks.
[08:36] Dr. Elena: We have a golden set of ~200 prompts, is that enough?
[08:42] Priya: That should be fine for initial regression; we do stratified sampling across entities to catch edge cases.
[08:52] Jordan: Next up—rollback playbook. The idea: automatic detection -> mitigation via fallback -> alert + postmortem. Detection signals: error rates, hallucination score bump, latency SLO breach.
[09:10] Marcus: how do you measure hallucination score automatically? We use heuristics but need to avoid false positives.
[09:18] Priya: We compute a similarity-based check vs. reference answers + heuristics on negation and entity hallucination, it's not perfect but effective to trigger investigation rather than immediate rollback unless severity is high.
[09:32] Dr. Elena: Would we be able to set thresholds? i.e., 10% increase in hallucination triggers canary rollback?
[09:40] Priya: Yes thresholds are configurable per-route.
[09:43] [10:00] Jordan: Let's talk about timeline — LumenHealth wants a decision by next Monday. We proposed two options: 1) Pin to rwd-7b family for two-week evaluation then freeze; 2) Pin to rwd-3b for lower cost and keep 7b as optional on high-risk prompts. Which is leaning?
[10:20] Dr. Elena: The clinical team favors option 1 but security wants written guarantees on audit and rollback speed.
[10:28] Sonia: Specifically we need request-level logs, user ids redaction policy, and confirmation that fallback events are recorded with original model id.
[10:36] Priya: All recorded. Fallback events include original model, chosen fallback, reason code, and a trace id that maps across systems.
[10:46] Marcus: for throughput, if we fallback during peak what happens to in-flight KV cache states? do we lose context?
[10:55] Priya: We preserve KV cache per session; when migrating to a smaller model we rehydrate a compatible prefix. In some edge cases we drop non-critical cache entries and flag the session. We'll note that in the playbook.
[11:20] Dr. Elena: ok, show us the exact fields in the audit log.
[11:26] Jordan: I'll attach the SOC2 appendix but quick list: request_id, timestamp, model_id, model_version, fallback_flag, fallback_model, reason_code, route, token_count, cost_estimate, user_id (hashed), truncated_input, confidence_scores where available.
[11:55] Sonia: Need to see retention SLA and export hooks to our SIEM.
[12:02] Jordan: we'll provide retention options: 30/90/365 days exportable via S3 or pushed to your SIEM.
[12:12] [12:12] Caleb: circling back to the decision matrix — we propose scoring: 40% clinical accuracy, 25% latency, 20% cost, 15% operational risk. You can tweak weights.
[12:29] Dr. Elena: That seems fair. We'll take it to the clinical PM and rank models.
[12:36] Tom: on the automation side, we want a test harness to run the golden set nightly and alert on drift. Can Redwood run that against canary?
[12:45] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize can schedule and run nightly regression and we can surface drift alerts into slack or pagers. We'll set up a channel.
[12:58] Marcus: do you have an example of the slack alert payload?
[13:02] Priya: I'll add an example in the follow-up.
[13:10] Dr. Elena: Anything else on rollbacks? We want runbooks for the SREs.
[13:16] Jordan: We'll provide runbook + playbook: commands to pin/unpin, to trigger full rollback, to force-route, and the postmortem template.
[13:28] Sonia: one last compliance note — encryption at rest keys and KMS integration for Private. Need confirmation of HSM support.
[13:36] Priya: HSM via your KMS provider is supported in Private mode; hosted uses Redwood-managed keys but we offer customer-managed keys for enterprise.
[13:44] Dr. Elena: good.
[13:50] Jordan: Alright to wrap: decision timeline, docs to share, and action owners. Caleb will synthesize and send internal recap.
[14:00] Caleb: I'll send a short recap and include the config snippet, and I will link pilot_results.csv and latency traces.
[14:08] Jordan: Great — thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

References in call: pilot_results.csv (link: https://drive.company/pilot_results.csv), rollout-playbook.md (link: https://docs.redwood.com/rollout-playbook), SOC2-appendix.pdf (link: https://docs.redwood.com/soc2-appendix).

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache), speaker overlap near minute markers, some proper nouns may be slightly off.
